page: Microsoft Azure F4-2ams_v7 is an AMD-based virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance configuration provides 2 dedicated vCPUs paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation density of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. This specification operates as a memory-intensive variant within the Fams_v7 series.

From a peripheral and I/O standpoint, the instance contains no bundled local disk storage and features zero GPUs. Host data persistence and temporary scratch storage depend on external disk attachments, supported by Premium Storage capability for remote block volumes. The network configuration provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating virtual network gateways or dedicated IP associations for external access.

The combination of dedicated CPU cores with elevated RAM density produces architectural advantages for software constrained by per-core commercial licensing. By limiting compute resources to 2 active vCPUs while retaining a 32.0 GB memory footprint, infrastructure costs associated with per-core software licensing remain controlled. The operational tradeoff is complete reliance on networked block storage for all disk I/O, which adds network overhead compared to instances with direct-attached local drives.

Microsoft Azure F4-2ams_v7 aligns with memory-intensive deployments that do not demand extensive parallel compute throughput. Representative use cases include mid-sized relational database systems, in-memory caching platforms, memory-heavy background ETL routines, and intermediate analytical data processing.
